item.title: Mega Move Update
item.description:
Sims and rankings have been updated to support the third Charged Move for Mega Evolutions. Pokemon which have had their Super Mega Raid debut automatically receive these attacks when they Mega Evolve. This attack has a bonus damage multiplier corresponding to the Pokemon's Mega Level - x1, x1.1, x1.2, to x1.3 at Mega Level 4. Mega Evolutions default to Mega Level 3 in the sims and rankings. You can set the Mega Level to a different value—note that Mega Level isn't currently preserved in links or custom groups.

Pardon the dust and good luck as the Mega Leagues arrive! I'll continue to update the site to support these features, and rest assured a new season preview is coming!

item.title: Mega Great, Ultra, and Master League Rankings
item.description:
Next week features Mega Evolutions in all three leagues! Most Megas have high Attack stats, so only a handful will be relevant in Great or Ultra League. In Great League, Mega Sableye is the standout choice with its higher stat product. In Ultra League, Mega Malamar and Altaria provide low cost ways to run these Pokemon. Mega Master League is where the real action is at, and you can expect it to play the same as earlier this season.

I've also added a QOL update to select Pokemon forms easier in simulations. For example, you can type "sab m" to select Mega Sableye, "sab s" to select Shadow Sableye, "zard x" to select Mega Charizard X, "zard y" to select Mega Charizard Y, or "zard n" to select normal Charizard.

item.title: Top Performers Update
item.description: The Top Performers page has been updated for all three leagues with teams and Pokemon from the past few months of training. Check it out if you need any team ideas as you battle on the road to Worlds! Training teams have also been updated to reflect the current meta. Good luck practicing!

item.title: Cramorant Sims and Rankings
item.description:
The simulations have been updated to incorporate Cramorant's new form change mechanics. Special thanks to the No Floats Left Research Group for their research! Here's a summary of Cramorant's exact mechanics:

- After Cramorant uses Dive or Surf, it reappears holding a certain prey depending on its HP remaining when it uses the move: Arrokuda (Gulping Form) if it has more than 50% HP remaining, or Pikachu (Gorging Form) if it has 50% HP remaining or less.
- Cramorant can't change prey if it's already holding one.
- Cramorant loses its prey if it switches out.
- When takes an unshielded Charged Attack while it's holding prey, it spits its prey at the attacker in a Gulp Missile attack. Cramorant fires Gulp Missile even if the Charged Attack damage will cause it to faint.
- Gulp Missile deals damage equal to 1 + 15% of the target's maximum HP, rounded down. For example, a Pokemon with 120 maximum HP takes 19 damage from Gulp Missile. Gulp Missile also lowers the target's Defense by 1 stage (Arrokuda) or the target's Attack by 2 stages (Pikachu).
- Gulp Missile's damage is unaffected by weaknesses, resistances, stats, or other multipliers.
- Gulp Missile can't be blocked (including by Mimikyu's disguise).
- Gulp Missile doesn't trigger an opposing Gulp Missile.
- If Cramorant KO's the target with Gulp Missile and also faints from the triggering Charged Attack, the result is a simultaneous KO, ie a draw.

Cramorant already draws comparisons to Pelipper, so with all of the above factored in, it rises to become the top Water/Flying pick. Gulp Missile softens many of its matchups, and even turns some losses into draws. The key is its quick pacing to ensure you have prey ready to retaliate. Because of this, Dive gains a slight edge over Surf even with its reduced power. Cramorant may take time to learn, so it's worth investing practice into its mechanics and matchups.

Here are a few strategies that Cramorant employs in the sims:

- Cramorant uses Dive or Surf to get its Gulp Missile ASAP, provided that Fly isn't a much more efficient use of energy.
- While Cramorant has prey, it tanks weak Charged Attacks so Gulp Missile fires earlier in the matchup rather than later.

Here are a few strategies that the sims employ against Cramorant:

- Opponents tank early Charged Attacks from Cramorant to save shields for when their Defense is dropped.
- While Cramorant has prey, opponents build up energy for back to back attacks to minimize the time they're debuffed.

Good luck with this wild new Pokemon and exploring its mechanics in depth!

item.title: Barraskewda Rankings
item.description:
Barraskewda is a glass cannon of a Water type. It has access to some good moves like Peck, Aqua Jet, and Close Combat for a mix of coverage, but all together, they're not enough to overcome its Haunter-level stat product.

If you're looking for sims and rankings on Cramorant, it has a unique form changing mechanic that will take some more time to investigate and code. Keep an eye out for an update!

Even without taking those mechanics into account, the floor for Cramorant's performance is somewhere close to Pelipper or Swanna—so at worst, a decent PvP addition. Make sure to catch and keep a few while the community tinkers with its strategy!

item.title: Thievul Rankings
item.description: Thievul gains Icy Wind this Community Day, propelling it to among the best Dark-type options in Great League. What it lacks in stats it makes up for in pressure, pacing, and new utility with Icy Wind's Attack drops. Time will tell if it has a lasting presence, but it should be a solid contender going forward. In Ultra League, it falls short due to its low CP. Have a great Community Day and look to add this one to your roster!

item.title: Scroll Cup Rankings
item.description: Scroll Cup picks up where Weather Cup leaves off with a Water-heavy meta and a handful of Electric counter options. This time, Dark types form the undercurrent, including Mandibuzz, Sableye, and Dark/Dragons, which gives Azumarill a larger role to play. Fighting has the most tenuous position in the cup. Still, a handful like Annihilape and Medicham may find unique roles.

item.title: Evolution Cup Rankings
item.description: Middle evolutions will be duking it out in the upcoming Evolution Cup. Well-known picks like Sealeo, Dusclops, Charjabug, and Primeape will be top contenders among a slew of Dragon types and a grab bag of Steels to fend them off. For those that can afford them, there are some truly spicy XL options like Morgrem and Tinkatuff which have no comparison. And the less said about Chansey, the better.

item.title: Weather Cup Rankings
item.description: Rain is in the forecast for Weather Cup next week. With Fire, Ice, Rock, and Water types, it's the Water types that rise above the rest. The most successful Pokemon will be Water types with non-Water offenses, and Pokemon that can hit the Water-types super effectively. While this cup has a sizeable pool, the meta is most likely to narrow to these powerhouse picks. Good luck and pack an umbrella!

item.title: Master Premier Rankings
item.description: Master Premier returns soon, largely unchanged from its last outing. Metagross, Florges, Dragonite, and Gyarados make up the power core of the cup. In support, Rhyperior looks to reclaim some of its standing with access to Drill Run. Primarina may prefer Waterfall over Charm now, where both variants performed about equally before. Gholdengo also improves thanks to the Shadow Ball buff, set to become a major player.

item.title: Retro Cup Rankings
item.description:
Retro Cup returns later this month with its usual roster of Dragon, Normal, Ghost, and Psychic types which tend to dominate the scene. Dragon is looking particularly fearsome with Kingdra, Sliggoo, and Shelgon bolstering double-Dragon strategies. The infamous Lickilicky will also be making yet another themed cup appearance alongside pretty much the full cast of Normal types, sans Wigglytuff. Ghost has the daunting task of competing against them without the benefit of Mimikyu or Aegislash, and may wreak havoc on their own ranks as Annihilape looks to dodge its more traditional counterparts.

Other notable Pokemon include Cradily, Grumpig, and a plethora of Ice types hoping to overcome the Dragons. Lapras is the bulkiest and most flexible of these, but Sealeo, Walrein, Aurorus, and Abomasnow could all find a place in the proceedings. Good luck and enjoy the brief break from the form-changing trio!

item.title: Ultra League Fantasy Cup Rankings
item.description:
The Ultra League edition of Fantasy Cup is charging onto the scene in the coming days, and it's a notably narrower cup than the Great League fare. Many of the latter's contenders carry a hefty price tag in Ultra League, while others can't compete at all.

Those looking for affordable team members can find them in Florges, Primarina, Togekiss, Empoleon, and a handful of others. At the very top of the tower, level 50 picks like Mimikyu, Galarian Stunfisk, Turtonator, and Corviknight look to overpower the meta. Their actual availability may make this meta unpredictable from the onset, so prepare for a broader initial set.

item.title: Mimikyu Rankings
item.description:
The new PvP system is now live in the core leagues, and with it, Mimikyu has been unleashed. Mimikyu's special ability blocks the first unshielded Charged Attack it receives, and then reduces its Defense by 1 stage for the rest of the match (even if it switches out).

With this extra shield, Mimikyu's 1v1 matchups are unprecedented - it effectively always has shield advantage. With Fairy and Ghost offenses, it can hit just about everything for neutral damage. Its worst matchups are against bulky Normal types, bonus points if they have Ghost coverage (you know who). This is an unexplored mechanic, so we'll see if it debuts to a hot start or takes some time to master like Aegislash.

NOTE: All simulations currently use the old/legacy PvP mechanics. I'll be exploring ways to implement a toggle or a cup-specific setting. If I don't find a good solution, I'll keep the legacy PvP mechanics in place until Worlds at the end of August. Stay tuned!

item.title: New Shadow Rankings
item.description:
New Shadow Pokemon are flocking this way, and they're well worth a look for PvP! Shadow Corviknight brings a notable boost to a Pokemon known for its tepid damage output. It's a top pick already, and should be dangerous in capable hands. Time will tell if it becomes preferred over the regular form!

Shadow Noctowl might have been scarier a few years ago, but it gives regular Noctowl access to Return. Not many Pokemon can make good use of this move, and Noctowl appears to be one of them, with good bulk, decent energy generation, and STAB.

Dewgong is too slow and dependent on its bulk to take advantage of the Shadow boost right now, but hold onto it for a future moveset shakeup. Shadow Dewgong has room to grow if Dewgong's pacing ever improves or if Icy Wind ever falls out of favor.

For Master League enthusiasts, Shadow Reshiram looks every bit as fearsome as its regular counterpart. Fusion Flare is even more devastating, and Draco Meteor is a practical OHKO against anything that doesn't resist it.

item.title: Summer Cup Rankings
item.description: Summer Cup returns in just over a week, and it should feel familiar for anyone playing along this season. Cradily, Lickilicky, and Furret return as top contenders, and are joined by a wave of Water types, including Kingdra, Empoleon, and Jellicent. Bug types provide a new angle to attack Cradily, in particular Forretress and Araquanid, so this cup should be a bit more open than Sunshine.
